<reason>Both sides built disciplined, closed-book cases with no fake sourcing, and both handled the Q/A format correctly. CON's frame was excellent: every vivid PRO example already contains an individually actionable artifact, so the motion's exclusive territory is the "residue" of sincere voices arriving at once, where coordination is only inferred from volume/timing/shared target — and where the harshest, fastest sanction is attached to the weakest finding. CON's calibration answer to the "you can't throttle a swarm you can't identify" pressure (remedy proportionate to confidence) was the single best defensive move in the debate, and the "immediate vs. human review" squeeze extracted a real concession. But PRO ultimately made the choice easier. PRO narrowed its test from the vulnerable "did nothing public to invite it" (which CON rightly attacked as grading deservingness) to a cleaner, workable line — "is this about what he did or where he sleeps" — which both answered the mass-flagging/brigading attack and excluded boycotts and #MeToo waves from the trigger, dissolving much of CON's residue worry. Then PRO closed the loop: CON's own enforcement of "hope she's home tonight" as intimidation "on its face" is only intelligible through the surrounding campaign, i.e., CON suspends for a post that is not explicitly threatening — the motion word for word. CON's final rejoinder ("judging a sentence by its thread is still judging the speaker's words") is a fair but asserted distinction that leaves PRO's catch largely standing. PRO also kept the irreversibility ledger alive (72 hours of lost sales vs. an archived address) against CON's freelancer scenario. CON retains a live proportionality route, which keeps this competitive rather than lopsided.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's closing re-reading of "hope she's home tonight": CON had called it intimidation "on its face" to keep the case inside a content-only rule, and PRO showed the sentence contains no threat or artifact and becomes hunting only through the coordinated context around it — meaning CON's own enforcement already suspends for non-explicitly-threatening posts, which is precisely the proposition.</best_rebuttal>
